SUMMARY

Eli Lilly and Company(LLY+6.55%)reported significant revenue growth driven by global demand for its incretin franchise and growth in its newest products across multiple therapeutic areas. Management stated that performance was bolstered by the rapid adoption of the Medicare GLP-1 bridge program and strong volume growth in international markets, particularly China. The company raised its full-year guidance to reflect these trends while continuing to invest in large-scale manufacturing expansions to support long-term supply needs. Strategic focus remains on advancing a broad clinical pipeline, including next-generation oral and injectable treatments for obesity and type 2 diabetes.

Operator:Ladies and gentlemen, thank you for standing by. And welcome to the Eli Lilly Third Quarter 26 Earnings Conference Call. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. Later, we will be conducting a question-and-answer session and instructions. Should you require operator assistance during the call, please press star, and an operator will assist you offline. I would now like to turn the conference over to your host, Michael Czapar, Senior Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Joining me on today's call are David A. Ricks, Lilly's chair and CEO; Lucas E. Montarce, chief financial officer; Dr. Daniel Skovronsky, chief scientific and medical officer; Adrienne Brown, president of Lilly Immunology; Dr. Carole Ho, president of Lilly Neuroscience; Ilya Yuffa, president of Lilly USA and global customer capabilities; Jacob S. Van Naarden, president of Lilly Oncology and head of business development; Patrik Jonsson, president of Lilly International; and Kenneth Custer, president of Lilly Cardiometabolic Health. During this call, we anticipate making projections and forward-looking statements based on our current expectations.

Our actual results could differ materially due to several factors, including those listed on slide 4. Additional information concerning factors that could cause actual results to differ is contained in our latest Form 10 ks and subsequent filings with the SEC. Our commentary will focus on our non GAAP financial measures. Now I will turn the call over to David.

David A. Ricks:Thank you, Mike. Q3 was another quarter of solid execution. We delivered strong financial results, raised our full year financial guidance, advanced our pipeline, and expanded our manufacturing footprint. Revenue grew nearly $7 billion compared to Q3 25. And our key product revenue increased by over 6 billion. Within key products, revenue from our oncology, immunology, and neuroscience portfolio doubled. Versus last year. We continued the global rollout of Foundayo, launching in The UK, Mexico, and Saudi Arabia for people with obesity, and in Mexico for people with type 2 diabetes. We achieved several key regulatory and pipeline milestones since our last call, including The US approval of our new weekly insulin and new indications for Inluriyo Jaypirca, and Mounjaro.

As part of the Medicare GLP-1 bridge program, we expanded access to obesity medicines in The US for approximately 20 million seniors. Since the July 1st launch, more than half a million people have filled a prescription for a Lilly medicine through this program. We have heard positive feedback from patients and physicians about the initial implementation. Within the GLP-1 bridge program, the Lilly portfolio is performing well. Among new bridge patients, 7 out of 10 starting on a Lilly obesity medicine. We are encouraged to see the strong uptake of the Bridge program, and believe it has the potential to both improve outcomes for seniors and save costs for Medicare.

A recently published paper from the University of Southern California's Schaeffer Center for Health Policy and Economics estimated the expansion of anti obesity medications in Medicare could deliver over $20 billion of cumulative savings over 10 years. This is an encouraging indicator of the magnitude of savings the GLP-1 bridge program could generate. We added to our pipeline through business development this quarter, acquiring AtaiBeckley and Merida Biosciences. We also progressed our manufacturing build out. To support our long term growth outlook. We broke ground on 2 new manufacturing facilities, a $6.5 billion facility in Houston, Texas and a $5 billion facility in Richmond, Virginia.

Distributed $1.5 billion of dividends in the third quarter and executed $400 million in share repurchases. We launched the Lilly Change the Course commitment, Through this new initiative, we set a new goal. Reach as many people in resource limited settings who have obesity and related diseases as in high income countries, prior to 2040. Lastly, we announced Patrik Jonsson, president of Lilly International, will retire at the end of 26. Ilya Yuffa will expand his responsibilities to include Lilly International as part of a newly created role. called president of Lilly Global Markets. I want to thank Patrik for his many contributions over a successful 36 year career at Lilly.

And now I will turn the call over to Lucas to review our Q3 results.

Lucas E. Montarce:Thanks, David. As shown on slide 7, Q3 was another quarter of industry leading financial results. Revenue grew 39% compared to Q3 25. Driven by Mounjaro, Zepbound, and a strong momentum across therapeutic areas and Gross margin as a percentage of revenue increased 80 basis points to 84.4%, as favorable product mix and an improved cost of production were partially offset by lower realized prices. Marketing, selling and administrative expenses increased 14% as we invested in promotional activities to support current and planned product launches. R&D expenses increased 23% driven by investment in our growing pipeline of early and late stage programs, and new molecules added through business development.

Our non GAAP performance margin was 54.2%, an increase of 5.9 percentage points from Q3 25 driven by revenue growth. Non GAAP earnings per share were $7.48 including acquired IPR&D charges of $4.57 This compares to $7.20 in Q3 25, which included $0.71 of acquired IPR&D charges. On slide 8, we quantify the effect of price, rate and volume on revenue growth. U. S. Revenue increased 34% in Q3, primarily driven by volume growth from Zepbound and Mounjaro. Partially offset by a 7% decline in price. US price benefited from a favorable adjustment to estimates from rebates and discounts. Excluding this adjustment, U.S. price declined 10%.

Europe revenue grew 29% in constant currency driven by sustained strong volume growth of Monjaro. Growth also benefited from a $410 million 1-time milestone payment related to charge ins. No additional charge ins milestone payment remains under our agreement with Beringer in Japan, revenue grew 26% in constant currency driven by Mounjaro and Kisunla. Mounjaro posted robust volume growth as share of new patient starts increased to over 50%. In China, revenue grew 62% in constant currency driven by the uptick of Mounjaro. Mounjaro is the first medicine in China to exceed $1 billion of revenue during its first full year.

In rest of the world, revenue grew 87% in constant currency driven by Mounjaro, primarily in Korea, Turkey and Brazil. Q3 revenue was positively impacted by approximately $900 million of previously mentioned items, including milestones and changes to estimate for rebates and discounts. On Slide 9, we provide an update on the performance of our key products. Within immunology, Ebglyss worldwide revenue grew 59% compared to Q3 25 in The U. S, Ebglyss continued to gain share of new prescriptions in the specialty dermatology market. And is the fastest-growing medicine in atopic dermatitis. In oncology, Jaypirca had another strong quarter, as worldwide revenue increased 59% compared to Q3 25.

In The US, Jaypirca was the fastest-growing BTK inhibitor as measured by total prescriptions. Inluriyo continued its impressive uptake in the metastatic breast cancer oral SERD market. Exiting Q3 with more than 60% share of new U. S. Prescriptions and 40% of US total prescriptions. In neuroscience, Kisunla revenue grew 175% compared to Q3 25. Kisunla maintained its leadership position in U. S. Amyloid targeting therapies. Diagnostic testing momentum continues to build. And the number of P-tau217 blood tests more than doubled compared to Q3 25. Translating to more people being diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease, and accessing treatment. Finally, in cardiometabolic health, Mounjaro and Zepbound combined for more than $16 billion of revenue.

Contributing $6 billion of growth compared to Q3 25. As seen on slide 10, total prescriptions in The U. S. Incretin market grew 32% compared to Q3 25. Oral GLP-1s and the Medicare GLP-1 bridge program are expanding the number of people taking incretin therapy. In The US, total incretin for obesity grew 82% in Q3, Approximately 6 out of 10 total prescriptions. And more than 7 out of 10 injectable prescriptions were for a Lilly medicine. In The US, type 2 diabetes incretin total prescription grew 8% compared to Q3 25. And the Lilly portfolio continues to lead here with more than 60% share of market. Outside The US, Lilly's portfolio again performed well.

Slide 11 shows aggregate trends in international incretins which have increased by 53% since the same period last year. As measured by IQVIA gross sales. Lilly strengthened its leadership position outside The U. S, gaining nearly 4 percentage points of share compared to Q2 26, to reach approximately 58%. Slide 12 provides an update on the Foundayo launch. In The US, total prescriptions and the share of new patients continue to rise. Approximately 4 in 10 patients starting an oral obesity medicine choose Foundayo. And the number of new Foundayo patients in Q3 doubled from the previous quarter. We look forward to launching Foundayo in type 2 diabetes in The U. S. And expect regulatory action in Q4.

Outside The US, Foundayo has launched in 4 countries and is under regulatory review in more than 40 additional countries. We continue to expect a global rollout in all major markets in 2027. On Slide 13, we provide an update on year to date capital allocation. Moving to Slide 14 is our updated 2026 financial guidance. Based on a strong underlying performance across our portfolio, we now expect full year revenue to be between $91 and $92 billion We saw strength in The U. S. Driven by rapid uptake of the Medicare GLP-1 bridge program. And outside of The US, from strong Mounjaro performance. Given our updated revenue outlook, we now expect non GAAP performance margin to be between 52.5%.

We expect non GAAP earnings per share of $35 to $36 This reflects an increase of $4.07 per share at the midpoint of the range before updates to the Q3 acquired IPR&D charges of $4.57 per share. We are pleased with our Q3 results and confident in our ability to deliver another year of industry leading growth. We will share our 2027 financial guidance on our Q4 call in January. However, I will share highlights on our initial thoughts regarding some of the pushes and pulls that we expect to impact our 2027 financial outlooks. Beginning with The US revenue, we expect sustained volume growth in the incretin market and the full year impact of the Medicare GLP-1 bridge access.

And the launch of Foundayo in type 2 diabetes. Outside The US, we expect Mounjaro's leadership position to continue. We expect to launch Foundayo, which will drive additional market growth. Consistent with previous years, we expect net realized price to be a headwind more than offset by volume growth. It is also worth noting that the 2026 revenue benefited from approximately $2 billion of 1-time items primarily related to milestones payments and changes in estimates for rebates and discounts that we do not expect to recur. Now I will turn the call over to Daniel to provide an update on our pipeline.

Daniel Skovronsky:Thanks, Lucas. Since our last earnings call, we have made progress across Lilly R&D. I will begin in cardiometabolic health. By recapping our most recent Phase 3 readout. From our GIP GLP-1-glucagon triple agonist, retatrutide. Just yesterday, we shared top line results from TRANSCEND T2D 2. A head to head trial of retatrutide versus semaglutide, in people with type 2 diabetes. As shown on slide 15, retatrutide delivered greater A1c reduction and more than doubled the weight loss of 2 milligrams semaglutide. Retatrutide reduced A1C by 2.2%, compared to 1.8% on 2 milligrams of semaglutide.

These data demonstrate retatrutide can provide even more glycemic control, than an approved diabetes medicine. providing a potential new treatment option. what is even more striking was the 20% to 21% weight loss achieved in people taking retatrutide compared to 9.4% weight loss in the semaglutide arm. For people with type 2 diabetes who struggle to lose weight, retatrutide continues to demonstrate powerful weight loss alongside compelling glycemic control in this difficult-to-treat population. Moving to another Lilly triple agonist, at last month's European Association for the Study of Diabetes meeting, we presented Phase 2 data for Olora-TZP. Olora-TZP is a combination of our selective amylin receptor agonist, eloralintide, and our GIP GLP-1 dual agonist, tirzepatide.

As shown on slide 16, Olora-TZP delivered weight loss of 23.3% at 48 weeks for people with type 2 diabetes and obesity. In a population that struggles to lose weight, this powerful combination delivered 57% more weight loss compared to tirzepatide. The world's most prescribed incretin. In addition, the highest dose combination of Olora-TZP delivered A1c reduction of 2.9%. At 48 weeks. And more than 3 out of 4 patients achieved an A1C below 5.7%, a level associated with normal blood glucose. Pending replication of these first of their kind results, in our Phase III trials, we believe this drug could meaningfully improve what is possible in the treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity.

And these data highlight the potential importance of treating with 3 physiologic hormones at once. Moving to slide 17. As 1 might expect, when rapidly escalating doses of a medicine with multiple mechanisms, the highest dose Olora-TZP arm had a higher discontinuation rate due to adverse events. As we move into Phase 3, we, of course, will use a slower, optimized dose escalation schedule. Which we anticipate will improve tolerability. Note that monotherapy of eloralintide showed excellent tolerability, with discontinuations due to adverse events lower than placebo. We look forward to beginning the Phase 3 trials of co formulated Olora-TZP imminently.

We also presented results from ACHIEVE-4, the cardiovascular outcomes trial, of orforglipron in people with type 2 diabetes and obesity with increased cardiovascular risk. As shown on slide 18, orforglipron met the primary endpoint of non inferiority versus insulin glargine. Reaffirming its cardiovascular safety profile. An additional prespecified analysis compared to insulin glargine orforglipron showed a 16% lower risk of MACE 4. And for people fortunate enough to have been randomized to receive orforglipron in this trial, there was a 57% lower risk of all cause death. These data complement the 6 previously presented Phase 3 trials for orforglipron and support the potential of orfagliptron as a foundational daily oral treatment.

For people with obesity and people with type 2 diabetes. Also in cardiometabolic health this quarter, in The US we received 2 important FDA approvals. The FDA approved tirzepatide to reduce cardiovascular risk in adults with type 2 diabetes. And the FDA approved our once weekly basal insulin, insulin efsitora alfa, for adults with type 2 diabetes under the brand name Onswik. Weekly basal insulin could significantly improve patient experience by reducing the number of injections compared to daily basal insulin. Moving to oncology. The FDA approved pirtobrutinib for certain patients with previously untreated CLL or SLL based on the Bruin CLL-313 Phase 3 trial. Pirtobrutinib reduced the risk of disease progression or death by 80%.

Compared to bendamustine plus rituximab. This approval underscores pirtobrutinib's versatility across the CLL continuum of care, It can now be used in the first line setting, for appropriate patients in addition to its valuable role in the relapsed or refractory post-covalent BTK inhibitor setting. The FDA also approved imlunestrant in combination with abemaciclib for ER-positive, HER 2 negative ESR 1 mutated advanced breast cancer. The all oral combination of imlunestrant and Abemaciclib gives patients a treatment approach that targets the 2 central drivers of ER positive breast cancer with an evidence based treatment approach. An established tolerability profile, and no new monitoring requirements.

We look forward to the results from EMBER-4 ongoing Phase 3 trial of imlunestrant in high risk early breast cancer. Elsewhere in oncology, we initiated a Phase 3 trial with our PI3 kinase alpha inhibitor tarsalisib, in combination with a CDK4/6 inhibitor and endocrine therapy in advanced breast cancer. Tarsalisib is a mutant selective PI3 kinase alpha inhibitor. Intended to target the PI 3 kinase mutations in breast cancer while sparing normal PI 3 kinase in healthy tissue. We believe this profile could lead to efficacy in the first line metastatic setting. Without as much of the toxicity as seen with other agents.

We now have 8 new oncology medicines or major new indications that are in Phase 3 trials or will start Phase 3 shortly. Moving to neuroscience. We completed the acquisition of AtaiBeckley, adding a portfolio of neuroplasticens with potential to treat depression, and other serious mental health conditions. We are pleased to welcome the AtaiBeckley team to Lilly and look forward to advancing multiple clinical programs together. Moving to immunology, we shared positive Phase 3 results for lebrikizumab in people with moderate to severe atopic dermatitis of the hands and feet. Hand and foot atopic dermatitis is painful and difficult to treat, and these data show lebrikizumab can be a new option for patients without the need for topical treatments.

We have submitted these data to the FDA for potential label update. We also shared 52-week results from phase 3b trials of ixekizumab and tirzepatide used together in people with psoriasis or psoriatic arthritis and obesity. The ixekizumab and tirzepatide arm delivered greater improvements in skin and joint outcomes than ixekizumab alone, Highlighting the importance of immunometabolic health. Earlier this month, we closed the acquisition of Merida Biosciences, which is developing MR511, a precision immunology therapy in Phase 1 for Graves' disease and thyroid eye disease. This drug was designed to selectively degrade the disease causing autoantibodies, while preserving normal immune function.

We are excited about the potential to help patients here and we are pleased to welcome the Merida team to Lilly. Slides 19 and 20 show pipeline movement since our last earnings call, and the key events we expect in the remainder of 2026. We look forward to sharing more details about our pipeline at the upcoming Lilly Innovation Day on December 7th. Although we will not have time to share everything we are working on, we will do our best to curate a few examples that illustrate the depth and breadth of our capabilities and our pipeline. At And I will turn the call back to David for closing remarks.

David A. Ricks:Thanks, Daniel. We were pleased with the progress in Q3 and throughout 2026. Delivered another quarter of strong financial results, advanced our pipeline through Lilly Research Labs and business development, and started building 2 new manufacturing facilities in The US to support our future growth. While we continue to make excellent progress during a period of industry leading growth, we remain focused on investing now to support our long term vision redefine how a pharmaceutical company can improve human health, at a global scale. We have developed differentiated capabilities in R and D, manufacturing, commercial operations. Where we are engaging directly with patients through platforms like Lilly Direct. Changing the way people access health care.

Given the depth of our incretin pipeline, we expect our leadership position in cardiometabolic health and broad pipeline of next generation obesity medicines to have a major impact on global health For decades to come. And with 3-fourths of our clinical pipeline focused on diseases outside of obesity, we are developing new medicines. That have the potential to impact a broad range of diseases, and deliver diversified, durable growth, for Lilly and our shareholders. Q3 was another strong quarter. Another step toward our long term goals. Now I will turn the call over to Mike to moderate the Q and A session.

Michael Czapar:Great. Thank you, David. We would like to take questions from as many callers as possible. So to that end, consistent with prior quarters, please limit yourself to 1 question. Operator, please provide the instructions for how to join the queue, and then we are ready for the first caller.

Or is this more of a pull forward of demand as we think about that kind of longer addressable TAM for the company? Thanks so much.

Operator:Yeah, Christopher, thank you for your question.

Lucas E. Montarce:And I think the starting point, if you go back when we set up the guide at the beginning of the year, you may remember that we have that slide with again, the opportunities and still events we had in front of us for 2026. We talked about the launch of Foundayo in Q2. We talked about starting the Medicare bridge program. You look at The US, and we are talking about 1 out of 10 patients that we are reaching nowadays, And in all US, we are talking about 2 patients out of 100 patients.

So it is actually a really low base, though the number seems really big, $16 billion this quarter of incretin business. The runway of opportunity for growth is still years to come from my perspective. And on top of that, we continue to expand the breadth across all the therapeutic areas. Super also happy to report the 100% growth on the rest of the key products across oncology, immunology, and neuroscience. So that is just to give you some color about the short term and how we think about also long term.

Michael Czapar:Great. Next question, please.

Geoffrey Meacham:I want to ask about what data you have on tirzepatide persistency in obesity just over the course of the past year or so. And importantly, when you look to next year, would you expect Foundayo and retatrutide to be different than that in terms of real world experience? Thank you.

Michael Czapar:Thanks, Jeff. To talk about tirzepatide persistency and obesity and thoughts on the pipeline looking in the future, we will go to Ilya.

And that was kind of the standard for chronic medicine for adherence, which ended up becoming around 16 to 18 months of adherence. What we are seeing with Zepbound is that in the covered space, we continue to see the trajectory of being just as beneficial in terms of adherence as we have seen in Trulicity. And even in the self pay, we are seeing that close to the covered market. So the persistency actually for chronic medication, Zepbound is doing extraordinarily well. Now expectations for oral, it is still early.

But as typical chronic medications has as well as if you take a look at orals, they typically are lower adherence overall relative to weekly injectable therapies. And that is what we expect to see. 1 additional data point I think will be important we look at even the success of Bridge, early days in Bridge, having a low out of pocket helps with that friction point, and we are seeing improved adherence in Bridge. So that will all play out as part of the different friction points, both in terms of out of pocket as well as the benefit that gain from these therapies.

Michael Czapar:Great. Thanks, Ilya. Next question, please.

Operator:Thank you. Our next question is coming from Seamus Fernandez with Guggenheim. Your line is live.

Seamus Fernandez:Oh, thanks so much. So I am gonna do the nonobesity question. is actually starting to show the prospect of becoming a blockbuster product and, you know, starting to grow faster, maybe a little bit faster overseas. But you know, I was hoping, Daniel, you might weigh in on the prospects for Trailblazer-3, the prospects for success, and how you see that program really evolving the treatment paradigm should it succeed. Particularly in the context of some of the novel tau biomarkers that we are starting to see. I think there are a lot of questions from investors that we get on what really is the market opportunity here.

Given the Kisunla uptake, but it does seem like some of those behaviors are changing. Thanks.

Michael Czapar:Great. Thanks, Seamus. Always welcome neuroscience questions. So we will go to Carol. Talk about prospects for Kisunla and maybe even kind of the neuroscience space more broadly? Yes. We are very excited to see the growth of Kisunla over the last year, and this growth is both driven by our confidence in this product with its convenient 30 minute infusion time, once monthly dosing, and the opportunity for treat to clear in the patient population. We have also seen a tremendous growth in the for diagnosis with blood based biomarkers with P-tau217 becoming available. And we see this becoming a diagnostic that enables access to early diagnosis, potentially even in primary care office in the future.

As we look at Trailblazer-3, which is our study looking at prevention in cognitively unimpaired people, looking at prevention of early symptomatic Alzheimer's disease, these biomarkers will certainly also enable early diagnosis for people that have risk concerns about their cognition before loss of their cognition. So we are excited both about the growth and early symptomatic Alzheimer's disease, but also if Trailblazer 3 reads out positively, really expanding this market to earlier stages of disease where we already have preliminary evidence from our early symptomatic Alzheimer's disease space that treating earlier will have a more significant impact on cognition. Thanks, Carol. Next question, please.

Operator:Thank you. Our next question is coming from Evan Seigerman with BMO Capital Markets. Your line is live.

Evan Seigerman:Hi, guys. Thank you so much for taking my question. Bigger picture 1 here So clearly, the incretin franchise is becoming an enormous earnings driver, but also raises the question of what comes next. When you look beyond the cardio. cardiometabolic disease, where do you see the best opportunity to build Lilly's next multibillion dollar growth pillar? And does recent BD activity suggests that neuroscience and immunology are emerging as higher strategic priorities? Thank you so much.

Michael Czapar:Great. Evan, for the question about the next big opportunity after incretin. So go to Daniel to talk about some of the pipeline opportunities he is excited about.

Daniel Skovronsky:Yeah. Thanks, Evan. I would say that we are excited about all 3 of our other therapeutic areas, which are immunology, neuroscience, and oncology. And the BD activity reflects just our strategic intent to grow those areas. But the intersection of that strategic intent with assets that are actually out there and that are attractive to us. Oncology is probably the space where we have made the most progress, we highlighted 8 really important late stage programs. Several of which could be quite large in size. For example, the recent Kelonia acquisition, which targets myeloma, is a huge opportunity if the data continue to hold out the way we expect them to.

Neuroscience, of course, is the area that has the largest unmet medical need and really the least progress in the pharmaceutical industry towards addressing that. We are firmly committed to making a difference for patients in this space, and you can see our acquisitions in sleep and psychiatry combined with our in house expertise in neurodegeneration are aimed to really grow that market on behalf of patients. And then finally, immunology. I think there is been a lot of crowding in immunology on a few probably important targets, but we also see great opportunity actually to raise expectations in immunology with breakthrough therapies that I think can deliver efficacy that is never been seen before.

And that is what we are trying to do with programs like the Merida acquisition, or the Orna acquisition, which is aimed at immune reset. So lots of growth opportunities across those areas.

Michael Czapar:Thank you, Daniel. Next caller, please.

Analyst:Thank you for taking my question. I wonder if you can speak a little more about Medicare Bridge. How does the split between injectable and pill and how does that mix look different from others? It seems by the majority of Medicare demand is injectable. I wonder if that surprised you with regard to your products in that space. We are seeing now that about 80% of the people getting treatment under bridge are naive or have not been on therapy in the past.

And so we see this as a significant driver of access long term, and it is still early days And while it is performing above our expectations, we see continued opportunity here to expand access and utilization and not only improve care of seniors, but, as we shared earlier, on independent study, also a potential of saving significant amount for Medicare overall.

Patrik Jonsson:Thank you very much. We have now launched in 4 markets outside The US. We started with UAE, very late in Q2, and the second half of Q3, launched in UK, Saudi, and Mexico. I would say that so far, the launch is very much in line with our expectations.
